reviewer: Separate Claude review agent, independent of the extractor; no human review claimed
scope: Independent review of the patient-RNA splicing use-case batch for use-case-patient-rna-splicing-validation: 441 records (348 results, 37 evaluations, 21 configurations, 11 claims including 7 relevance judgements, 9 methods, 7 protocols, 4 datasets, 4 sources). The three article XMLs and the Drost Data S1 workbook were re-downloaded and match their recorded SHA-256; the two archived copies decompress to the same bytes. All 348 results were re-read with a separate parser (the extractor's scripts were not run) and match. Changes are listed in docs/reviews/use-cases/patient-rna-splicing-validation-2026-10-09.md.
limitations: Automated review by a Claude agent; not human scientific review, not reproduction of any tool and not clinical validation.
Figures, Drost Data S1 Tables S1, S2, S5 and S6, and Segers Additional file 1 were not checked.
The AbSplice preprint and other screened sources in research.md were not re-read.
Judgement pins are not set; they are computed by the integrator after the records are in the store.

Identical Pangolin, SPiP and SpliceAI rows are consistent: Entire minus In House gives the same CAGI6 counts (32 TP, 16 TN) for all three. Not disputed.
relevance direct changed to proxy (DNA-only predictors, which the use case's output keeps as a separate proxy; Segers gene ranks mix expression and splicing defects and are developer-run).

source caveats added to limitations (truth method, author-devised consensus rule, prose slips, Pangolin version, Segers truth-set origin and developer-run comparators, Segarra-Casas cohort size and 66.6% figure).
source_locator paragraph numbers corrected (Discussion paragraph 5; Discussion paragraphs 5 and 10); claims.csv updated.
